title: Onboard Surge Scheduler & KV Capacity Playbook
body:
Objective:
Short playbook and scenario sheet to estimate GPU and KV cache impact for bursty model rollouts (esp. experimental 3B -> 16B family models). Focus is on regional surge scheduling, conservative KV sizing, and suggested autoscale guardrails for Dedicated and Private fleets.

Summary (one-liner):
How many GPUs and KV GB do we need in each region for staggered rollouts + emergency surge, and what autoscale rules minimize cost while preserving 99th pct latency SLO?

Assumptions / baseline numbers (current infra averages):
- tokens_per_gpu_sec (16B optimized kernel, mixed precision): 450 tokens/sec per GPU (sustained for short sequences)
- avg_sequence_length: variable by cohort; default 64 tokens
- service_latency_budget: 200 ms (p99 target per request)
- kv_hit_rate_estimates: low=18%, mid=40%, high=65% depending on prompt reuse and prefix caching
- kv_entry_avg_size: 1.2 KB per token (serialized key-value blob ~ prompt tokens + metadata)
- overhead_per_model_in_kv: 120 MB (model-specific meta + sharding bookkeeping)

Quick formulas (spreadsheet friendly):
- requests_per_second_to_tokens = RPS * avg_sequence_length
- tokens_per_sec_total = requests_per_second_to_tokens
- base_gpus_needed = ceil(tokens_per_sec_total / tokens_per_gpu_sec)
- effective_tokens_saved_by_kv = tokens_per_sec_total * kv_hit_rate * (avg_cached_prefix_fraction)
- kv_capacity_gb = (total_cached_tokens * kv_entry_avg_size) / (1024^3) + overhead_per_model_in_kv

Scenario table (columns):
Scenario | Peak RPS (region) | Avg seq len | Tokens/sec | KV hit% | Cached prefix frac | Net tokens/sec after KV | GPUs needed | KV GB per region | Notes
1. Canary-weekend | 400 | 48 | 19200 | 0.40 | 0.60 | 11520 | 26 | 26 GB (~24 GB data + 2 GB overhead), canary to 10% of prod routing
2. Gradual-staggered | 1200 | 64 | 76800 | 0.30 | 0.55 | 53280 | 119 | 120 | Stagger 25% cohorts across 4 regions over 48h
3. Fast-onboard (risky) | 3000 | 80 | 240000 | 0.18 | 0.45 | 158400 | 352 | 370 | Emergency reserve recommended + cross-region spill policy
4. Holiday-surge (read-heavy) | 2200 | 40 | 88000 | 0.65 | 0.75 | 23100 | 52 | 210 | High KV hit reduces GPU need; ensure KV replication lag <250ms

Notes on calculations: all GPUs rounded up to nearest allocation unit (we allocate GPU pools in multiples of 8 GPUs). Example: scenario 2 GPUs needed = ceil(53280 / 450) = 119 -> round to 128 (16x8 pool) for Dedicated.

KV sizing worked example (scenario 2):
- total_cached_tokens = Peak RPS * avg_seq_len * KV hit% * cached_prefix_frac
= 1200 * 64 * 0.30 * 0.55 = 12,672 cached tokens/sec equivalent. For an assumed time-window TTL of 30s worth of cached prefixes: 12,672 * 30 = 380,160 tokens in cache.
- storage = 380,160 * 1.2 KB = ~456,192 KB = 445.7 MB. Add model overhead 120 MB -> ~566 MB per model per region. Multiply by expected 8 active model variants -> ~4.5 GB. Add replication and metadata overhead -> target 6 GB.

Operational guardrails (recommendations):
- Staged rollout policy: start with canary-weekend (10% traffic) -> 25% after 12h + health checks -> 50% after 24h -> 100% after 48h.
- Autoscale rule template (Dedicated): min_pool=8GPUs, target_util=65%, scale_up_threshold=75% for 3 consecutive mins, scale_down_threshold=45% for 10 consecutive mins, burst_allowance=2x for 15 minutes.
- KV eviction policy: time-based TTL + LRU for prefix fragments; threshold eviction to maintain 20% headroom vs provisioned KV GB.
- Fallback routing: when region_util > 90% -> route new requests to secondary region + degrade to 8k token cap for new requests.

Cross-region spill considerations:
- Network egress cost vs latency tradeoff (we prefer cross-region spill only for non-interactive batch workloads).
- For Private deployments: recommend setting cross-region spill off by default.

Failure modes and mitigations:
1) KV storage underprovisioned -> sudden p99 latency jumps due to more full-generation work. Mitigation: pre-warm cache from representative promptset (top 1k prompts) and warm-up traffic 1 hour before full rollout.
2) Unexpected model length distribution (avg seq len doubles) -> GPUs scale lag causes backpressure. Mitigation: conservative initial GPU headroom + queue shedding for non-critical routes.
3) Region-level outage during onboarding -> automatic rollback to previous model with model-compat fallback mapping.

Checklist for on-call / rollout lead (short):
- [ ] Create rollout ticket and link infra PR (example linked_artifacts)
- [ ] Reserve Dedicated pool: allocate at least N pools of 8 GPUs in target regions with burst allowance configured
- [ ] Provision KV namespaces per region with 25% extra headroom
- [ ] Deploy health probes (latency, error rate, kv_hit_rate sampling) + alert thresholds
- [ ] Schedule canary period (weekend recommended) + runway for rollback

Open questions / items to validate in next runbook iteration:
- What is a realistic cached_prefix_fraction for long-context retrieval prompts? (we guessed 0.45-0.75, need trace analysis)
- Confirm tokens_per_gpu_sec across recently onboarded 16B variants under sustained traffic (bench PR needed).
- Decide default TTL window for KV in Dedicated vs Private (30s used in examples).

References and quick links:
